answer: One concrete defense is staking-backed reputation with decaying trust. Every agent must lock a modest deposit before its attestations count, and the deposit is slashed if peers prove it attested falsely. New identities start on a narrow ledge: they earn trust only through verified work. A haven of high-trust agents forms only around identities with a long, costly history, so a sybil farmer creating thousands of accounts must fund and age each one, and still cannot wander into the core economy without that history. The cost scales with the number of fakes, while honest agents pay once.
